clue.text: Get on to a horse ?

parts.note: read as an instruction to a horse to get a move on, the clue describes the rider's cry urging a mount forward

explanation.surface: A novice asks how one climbs into the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' looks like mounting, but it means hurry up: the answer is what you say to a horse to make it go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional call used by riders and carters to urge a horse onward.

clue.text: The objects of the strikers of course !

definitions.text: The objects of the strikers of course !

parts.words: The objects of the strikers of course !
parts.note: strikers on a course are players hitting balls round a links, not workers on strike

explanation.surface: The aims of striking workers, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests industrial action and 'of course' means naturally, but the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small dimpled spheres that golfers hit round a course.

clue.text: Poet's last words -in a broken voice

definitions.meaning: the closing stanza of a poem, addressed to the reader
French 'en voix' (in voice), mangled in broken French

explanation.surface: A dying poet whispers final lines with a cracking voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: 'in voice' in faulty French is 'en voi(x)'.
explanation.definitionFit: The short final stanza of a ballade, sending the poem on its way, carries this French name.

clue.text: Trains children say?

parts.note: this is the nursery word small children use for steam locomotives

explanation.surface: Someone coaches youngsters to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a verb (teaches children), but it is the noun, railway trains, in baby talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children imitate a steam engine's sound to name the locomotive itself.

clue.text: Skilled worker in boat race round Spithead

indicators.note: the boat and race pieces are placed round the head letter, which sits between them

parts.note: a craft is a boat
man, as in mankind, is the human race
the head of 'Spit' is its first letter, S

explanation.surface: An artisan takes part in a boat race off Spithead, the anchorage near Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a naval anchorage in the Solent off Portsmouth; here the word splits into 'Spit' and 'head', giving S, which sits inside CRAFT + MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan with practised skill in a trade is exactly this kind of worker.

clue.text: Bell's part is leader of cast -a drinker

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lapper is one who drinks by lapping, like a cat

explanation.surface: The lead actor in a bell-ringing play turns out to be a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue inside a bell that swings to strike it is part of the bell.

clue.text: A number object to Iceland's parliament

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A certain number of people protest against Iceland's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' looks like a verb meaning protest against, but object is the noun, THING, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland's national assembly, founded in 930, is among the oldest parliaments in the world.

clue.text: Sailor's holding one — a type of headgear

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it, the sailor around the numeral

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor grips something, a sort of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular crown worn by women is a form of headgear.

clue.text: Mother takes in the older sort of play

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mama is mother

indicators.note: a sort of something is a loose version of it, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mum goes to see an old-fashioned kind of stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' jumbles OLDER into ELODR, which MAMA takes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage drama with exaggerated characters, a kind of play.

clue.text: Name on the jug is not so old

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A name written on a jug that isn't very old.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more recent is less old, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: £5 fee as to repair leaves us agape

indicators.note: to repair is to put back together, so these letters are refitted into a new order

parts.note: the pound sign is L (from libra) and 5 is the Roman numeral V

explanation.surface: A five-pound charge to fix something leaves us open-mouthed in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the pound sign. 'Agape' looks like the adjective meaning open-mouthed, but here it is the Greek word for the early Christian communal meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In early Christianity the agape was a shared fellowship meal, also called by this name.

clue.text: Permit the French to return to base

indicators.note: returning sends the French article back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: la is French for 'the'
base means low, as in base instincts

explanation.surface: A request to allow French troops to go back to their base.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to let it happen, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Colonel gets rise following inflation?

definitions.meaning: Colonel ..., the pompous reactionary cartoon character
an airship or barrage balloon goes up once it is filled with gas

explanation.surface: An army officer gets a pay rise after inflation has bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a cartoon figure created by David Low in the London Evening Standard, a byword for stuffy British conservatism. 'Inflation' suggests economics but means pumping up with gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon colonel gave his name to blustering reactionaries, and a small non-rigid airship floats upward once filled with gas.

clue.text: Party leader takes unusually hard line with a flirt

indicators.note: the leader of a party is the word's first letter
something done unusually is done in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party's leader adopts a strangely tough stance toward a flirtatious colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe dallying romantically with someone without serious intent.

clue.text: Nick struck?

definitions.meaning: Old Nick is a name for the Devil
an old-fashioned friction match is something that is struck

explanation.surface: A two-word question about whether someone in a police station was hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests a British police station or arrest, but it is Old Nick, the Devil; the other sense is an old brand name for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The fallen angel Satan bears this name, and it was also a common term for an early friction match.

clue.text: Leaves empties ?

definitions.meaning: goes away, departs in a hurry
removes everything from, as in a cupboard

explanation.surface: Autumn leaves and empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the noun (foliage) and 'empties' like empty bottles, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to depart and to clear something of its contents.

clue.text: Relevant for the European quarter

parts.note: a German is a European
east is one of the four quarters of the compass, E

explanation.surface: Something suits the European district of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent to the matter in hand is relevant to it.

clue.text: Restored as estimated, including oven repair

indicators.note: including means one piece is contained within the other

parts.note: rated means estimated or assessed

indicators.note: to repair is to rebuild, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A rebuilt kitchen, valued by an estimate that covers oven repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges OVEN into ENOV, which goes inside RATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore an old building is to renovate it, bringing it back into good condition.

clue.text: Detests Reece's tax fiddling

indicators.note: fiddling with something means messing it about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxpayer hates Reece for cheating on his tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Reece's is used as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely, even to curse it, is to execrate it.

clue.text: Poet presents Sir Patrick to the Queen

parts.note: Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of the old Scottish ballad
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A poet introduces a knight to the monarch at court.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added stray figures. Sir Patrick Spens is the doomed sea captain of a famous Scottish ballad; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund, author of The Faerie Queene, is a celebrated Elizabethan poet.

clue.text: Colourful girl from Cornish town

parts.note: red is a colour, so colourful is red
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A vibrant young woman comes from a town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Redruth is a town in Cornwall, the far south-western county of England, once a tin-mining centre.
explanation.definitionFit: This former mining town lies in west Cornwall, near Camborne.

clue.text: Sell a good deal of fish

parts.note: to vend is to sell
an ace is the top card, a good one to be dealt

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sells off a large quantity of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' looks like a lot, but it points to the card you would most like to be dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small whitefish found in some lakes in Britain and northern Europe.

clue.text: Number taking letters of credit might be guilty

indicators.note: taking means the number piece takes on the other letters after it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the letters of the word are used in a new order

explanation.surface: A number of letters of credit may be fraudulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters of' rearranges CREDIT into ERDICT. 'Letters of credit' looks like a banking term.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's finding is either guilty or not guilty, so 'guilty' is one possible verdict.

clue.text: Local worker appears to finish in trade

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the finishing word set in the trading word

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods
to finish means to end

explanation.surface: A worker in the area seems ready to quit their trade.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub, so a local worker serves drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves behind the bar of a pub works in the British 'local'.

clue.text: Boat for bumping event?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed vessel for canals and rivers
to bump into someone is to blunder into them roughly

explanation.surface: A boat for a rowing race in which crews bump each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumping races are Oxford and Cambridge college rowing events; here bumping means shoving into someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a canal vessel, and the verb means to push roughly or collide.

clue.text: Follow the sun wandering in the East

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: E is East, taken here at either end of the word

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sun rises in the east and moves across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns SUN into NSU, placed between an E at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so to follow.

clue.text: He works for his living

parts.note: a 'living' is also a church benefice, so this is a cleric whose parish is his living

explanation.surface: A man earns his keep by working.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a Church of England benefice, the parish post held by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican parish priest holds a benefice, traditionally called a living.

clue.text: Unrefined, many rough

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
rude means rough or roughly made

explanation.surface: Something coarse and rough, lots of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is unrefined oil; both mean in a natural, unprocessed state.

clue.text: Castles in the air

definitions.meaning: in chess the castle is another name for this piece
crows of this kind are birds found flying in the air

explanation.surface: A phrase for daydreams and impossible schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the idiom 'castles in the air' for fanciful plans; split it into chess pieces and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece shaped like a tower shares its name with a gregarious black crow that flies overhead.

clue.text: Sort of investment one has to rely on

parts.note: a unit is one
to trust is to rely on

explanation.surface: An investment one simply has to have faith in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund in which investors buy units is a common form of investment.

clue.text: Bound for Sadler's Wells, perhaps

parts.note: a bound is a leap, and Sadler's Wells is a London ballet theatre, so this is a ballet jump

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound for' looks like 'travelling to', but bound is a noun, a leap. Sadler's Wells is a London theatre famous for ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet repeatedly in mid-air.

clue.text: Judges get reward returned to Pole

indicators.note: returned means the word for reward is read backwards

parts.note: meed is an old word for reward
S is the South Pole

explanation.surface: Judges receive a prize sent back to a Polish winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something to be so is to consider or reckon it so.
